txt: *chews loudly*
...then suddenly he leans forward and uses the 0-end of the measuring tape to nudge his opponent's balls further from the small brown sphere in the pit. As he does this, he complains about his back.
A heavy silence falls over the crater. The man in the checkered suit doesn't know where to look or what to do with his hands. Finally he speaks:
Gaston glumly stares at the shot put ball. Several seconds pass. Then he speaks: "It's too late now, officer... you got back too late. René is gone."
Gaston sighs and mumbles, more to himself than you: "Hell, most likely. He was an absolute cunt..."

He looks at you for a moment and then speaks quietly. "I took them for myself. Took them to remember that old cunt. Nobody knew him better than I did, and I want to remember that old cunt by something."
He nods, understanding the finality of the situation, and hands you the sandwich. "Please... just take it slowly. Give her the attention she deserves."
He stares at you, aghast. "What a waste..."
His merry partner is staring at the ground like he's trying to see right through to the other side.
His voice trembles. "...a-and she never lost sight of it. And I thought if the most beautiful being in the world can love him, then there must be something worth holding on to..."
The jolly-looking man in the checkered jacket moves lazily. Like a giant tomcat stretched out in the sun...
The man looks at his partner with suspicion, then his eyes light up, he pockets the sandwich and chuckles. "*Merci beaucoup, Capitaine Arnoux*!"
The old man looks devastated as he observes you and René strengthen your  manly bond over his culinary wonder.
The old man nods and turns away from you.
The old man stares at the flower, then sighs and says: "René wasn't really what you'd call a botanist, officer. And believe me, he didn't like Insulindian Lilies."
The sandwich owner looks at you, eyes filled with anguish. "You're describing prison food, officer. I like different, *better* food. Fine dining, not *jailtime*. Please, just drop it."
The scepticism emanating from the merry senior could be sensed all the way to the Semenine Isles.

"'In Guillaume's time you'd have been shot without a trial'. That's what he said to me." The old man gathers himself and wipes his eyes again. "He lived a cunt and he died a cunt. Let's leave it at that."
"*Capitaine Arnoux -- le fléau des chevaux*!"
"*Ce serait délicieux*! he shouts excitedly. "Can you make that sandwich, officer?"
"*Mon dieu*, officer!" He looks at your wounds. "It is worse than I thought! Believe me, I know all about that kind of pain, I've had hip trouble for the past... week."
"*Mon dieu*, that is an excellent idea!" he exclaims. "That would virtually negate the component loss."
"*Mon dieu*, the pain is exceptionally bad today..."
"*Mon dieu*, you set it on fire!" He looks at the plaza. "What kind of a policeman are you?"
"*Mon dieu*," the jolly man exclaims. "Good job, officer. That was an excellent throw!"
"*Pardon*, René," he quickly turns back to you. "We must pick this up later, I'm helping the officer right now."
"*So* weird... what was that, officer?" The old man is visibly shaken, but tries to force a smile. "Actually, *please*, let's talk about something else."
"Actually never mind... Wouldn't be the same..."
"Ah, *mon dieu*! The pain in my back is unbearable. I can't even say if it's in my back or hip anymore. Feels like it's in *both*!" He tries to measure the throw.
"Already forgotten, officer."
"Alright, alright," the old man is taken aback by René's commanding tone, but dares not dispute him. "I have a bad feeling about this."
"Alright." The jolly man smiles. "Let's hear them, officer."
"And that even whilst crawling with a mangled half-dead prince on his back, he still managed to murder three rebels on his way."
"And the worst part of that, officer," he says, face terrified, "is having to spend your days playing pétanque with an angry snake."
"Apocalypse?" He backs away, visibly worried. "I uh... I don't know, what this means, officer. I'm sorry. But thank you! I'm here to cooperate any way I can."
"Argh.. my back! I swear it's getting worse..."
"Believe me, officer, I wish I could help you, but I need this sandwich to keep my blood sugar stable." He's squirming, avoiding your gaze. "In my age you need to pay attention to these things."
"Blood ground..." The other one shakes his head. "You got old René going there. Like he isn't angry enough already..."
"But *not* with a monetary pension unfortunately," the checkered suit snaps at his partner and turns to you. "What can I do for you, officer?"
"But don't worry, I'm sure there's something else old René or I can assist you with."

"But it wasn't the revolutionaries that *sullied* the idea for you, was it?" He looks at the old soldier almost gently. "She gave them to me too and your jealous little heart just couldn't accept it."
"But you probably had some official business too?" he asks and puts the hat back on.
"Can I at least finish my fucking sentence before you piss on it? Is that okay, René?" His eyes are furious. "I'm not anyone important in the Union. I just know Evrart."
"Coming from an officer of the law, this appraisal means an awful lot to me." He bows slightly. "Thank you."
"Departed," his partner finishes his sentence, then chuckles: "Until the very end she couldn't decide between us. The most indecisive woman I've ever met."
"Don't get started on that again. What happened, happened." There is some weariness in his voice now -- he's heard this rant many times before.
"Don't you mean Frissel the Fun?"
"Easy now, René." He snickers. "I *will* join the seniors swimming class later, but right now I don't want to keep the officer waiting -- police business is usually urgent."
"Easy, René, take it easy." There's genuine concern in his face. "You're right, absolutely right. What was, *was* and that's it. Isn't that right, officer?"
"Ee... okay, sure sure, I'm not worried. We're here all the time. Every day. Impossible to miss us, officer."
"Ee... okay, sure sure," he quiets you. "Everybody wins, but is there anything I can help you with right now to *speed up* the process?"
"Eh... I don't think that's gonna happen." He chuckles. "Why would you even...?"
"Enough, officer," the other one says with surprising resoluteness. "We can't help you. Not with this. Such an *emotional* topic..."
"Everyone in Martinaise knows the Claire brothers," he says solemnly. "I taught these boys human studies and history in the gymnasium."

"Evrart *created* this job for René, because he knows the Royal Carabineer's pension of honour and PTSD isn't something a man can live off. 'A decorated kingsman collecting tare reflects bad on the whole neighbourhood.' -- his words."
"FUCK OFF, it's mine!" He jerks away, immediately startled by his own reaction.
"Ghost of the past." The old man removes his hat and sea wind ruffles his grey hair. "Everyone in this story is already dead, officer. I don't wanna talk about them."
"Guess he was about to head home, 'cause when the dockworkers found him he was wearing civilian clothes and not the cockatoo uniform I saw him in all the time."
"Guess he was about to head home. The dockworkers found him in his civilian clothes and not the cockatoo uniform you... ugh... confiscated."
"Have the days always been this long?"
"He saved some *maudit* princeling who foolishly strolled into the front line in his gown of velvet and gold."
"Heck," he says with a chuckle. "*Technically* we're both still engaged to her."
"Hello, officer." He turns to you. "How might I be of assistance on this fine day?"

"His angry little heart finally gave out." He sighs. "The dockworkers found him in the guard booth this morning. Wasn't even supposed to be working for another week, but he just had to prove how tough he is..."
"How did *you* find the story to be, officer?"
"How long have we known each other? Almost eighty years?"
"Huh?" The jolly man is scratching his head in bewilderment. He doesn't understand the situation.
"I believe everyone has the right to think and do whatever they want. Even if it's nothing at all. I'm very *adaptable*."
"I could, but I'd rather not." He smiles. "I don't want to take up your time with trivial details, officer."
"I don't eat worker-food!" he blurts out, immediately regretting it. "Look, officer, I like different, *classic* food. Fine dining, not *worker backs*. Please, just drop it."
"I don't even consider myself a regular socialist. Politics is not really something I involve myself in, officer."
"I don't understand, René..." He looks around with an expression of complete bafflement.
"I don't want to," he argues, glancing at you worriedly. "Look, officer, I like different, *classic* food. Fine dining, not soil. Please, just drop it."
"I guess in the end the Insulindian Lillies were just another piece of the Old Insulinde, the royalists had to surrender to the Mazovian insurgents. It doesn't really matter anymore."
"I guess it doesn't really matter anymore. You do what you have to, like the rest of us... So how can I help?"
"I guess you don't really need taste buds for police work." He looks disappointed. "Is there anything else, officer?"
"I have really outdone myself..." He takes a bite out of his sandwich. "This is divine."
"I hope you are not just tricking an old man out of the little he has left." He says solemnly and hands you his sandwich.
"I just don't know anymore... about anything really." He slowly shakes his head, then remembers your presence. "But you... you must need something?"
"I know what you mean, officer," he says excitedly. "Then there's the blood sugar and don't even get me started on the bladder troubles..."
"I prefer *highly-adaptable* myself," he chuckles merrily. "Has a better ring to it, don't you think?"
"I really don't understand how my sandwich could..." he starts, but falls silent.
"I repeat -- an *absolute* cunt." He turns to look at the crater. "Even his old army buddies didn't want him around. He was like an old viper."
"I should be hungry -- why am I not hungry?"
"I uh..." He rubs his chin, not knowing what to say. "That's nice. Uh... If I'm in your way, I'll move! Or can I help in any way?"
"I uh..." He rubs his chin, not knowing what to say. "That's nice. Uh... better somehow. Can I help in any way?"
"I understand the situation," he says quietly and hands you the sandwich. "Please... just take it slowly. Give her the attention she deserves."
"I wish I could, but I just don't know anything." His cheeks turn red. "I always keep my nose clean and don't gossip. Everyone knows and respects that."
"I wonder if Leo knows pétanque..."
"I would rather just have this one, officer." He's avoiding your eyes. "It's really good."
"I'll be with you in a moment, officer. Let me just finish my sandwich." He nods to his partner. "Talk to angry old René first."
"I'll just measure... *ouch*. I can barely move..."
"I'm *not*," he assures you. "I'm not even anyo---"
"I'm glad to assist you if I can, officer," he replies, voice tired and breaking.
"I'm listening, officer." He nods.
"I'm sorry, officer, I just..." He dries his eyes. "Thank you, *thank you* for this little memorabilia. It really means the world to me."
"I'm sorry, officer, but I really don't share food," he says and quickly adds: "Nothing personal, it's just a principle."
"Is there anything I can do for you right now?" he asks. "Maybe to speed the whole process up a bit?"
"It is such a pleasure to see you again, officer. How may I aid the Citizens Militia on this fine day?"
"It is what it is, part of life really," he mumbles, only half-listening to you. "But to know someone for 79 years, then one day they're just *gone*..."
"It is what it is... part of life," he mumbles, only half-listening to you. "But to know someone for 79 years, then one day they're just *gone*..."
"It was quite funny, officer." He lets out a keen laughter. "I thought it was very funny."
"It's okay, officer. Forgotten completely. It was my *boule* and I have a spare." He produces another ball from his pocket. "Everything is good and we're ready to assist any way we can!"
"It's okay, officer." He smooths his white whiskers. "You might have just saved René from a heart attack."
"It's really not." He turns to René. "Please do spare us the cocaine fairy tales."
"It... isn't right." The old man doesn't even bother looking away. "René wanted to be buried in his uniform. But I guess it doesn't matter now..."
"Just easier that way," he nods in approval. "Besides, life isn't as black and white as René's of the World try to make it seem. It's all shades of grey really."
"Keep it, it's not even a real *boule*." He waves you away. "Besides, it doesn't really matter now. I've never seen anyone else play pétanque in Martinaise."
"Lately my eyes just aren't the same and even getting out of the bed is pretty difficult..."
"Let me see..." Gaston takes the photo, hands trembling. "This was 60 years ago! We all went to that parade. Young René looks so happy and Jeannie..." Eyes blurry with tears, he has to stop.
"Let me think..." He looks at the clouds, wistfully. "I heard someone was hanged and left on a tree for a week, but that's all I know really."
"Life... *mnjam-mnjam*... doesn't need to be a struggle." He covers his mouth to hide a burp.
"Like what, officer?" His eyes rest on the sandwich. "This is as good as they come in Revachol, I assure you."
"Look, officer," his partner jumps in. "The container yard doesn't actually need a guardsman. Never had one before René. Mr. Claire had that booth built specially for him. It's mostly *decorative*."
"Maybe fishing... or crossword puzzles?"
"Maybe it's time to slow down, enjoy life a bit?" He smiles apologetically. "Anything I can do to assist you?"
"Maybe, maybe, but also bear in mind, officer..." He points to the sun-shaped medal on René's chest. "They don't hand these out for anyone with a service record."
"Mhmh," he replies with a slight nod. "That's their old name, dating back to the time of kings and crests and all that other stuff he loved so much."
"Never thought I'd miss that angry prick..."
"No, I'm sorry, officer." he shakes his head. "I don't even have a keycard. Evrart usually sends someone to get me, when he wants to talk."
"No, everything would fall off," he argues, glancing at you worriedly. "Look, officer, I'm not a miner. I like different, *tasty* food. Fine dining, not coal. Please, just drop it."
"No, officer." He shakes his head meekly. "We can't help you with that, maybe there's something else we *can* help you with?"
"No, officer." The culinary genius shakes his head with unexpected resolve. "Please let it go, It's making me really uncomfortable."
"No, officers, I'm sorry. And I really *would* like to assist," he adds, smiling apologetically. "You are both good guys. I can see that."
"No," he replies quickly. "René was the most stubborn man in Revachol. Nothing you or I could say would ever *push* him to do anything. The man was completely immovable."
"No-no, officer! René doesn't know what he's saying." The jolly one jumps in.
"Not bad, René, you might stand a chance this time."
"Not in the technical sense..." His eyes fix on the boules in the crater. "I don't have a vote or a membership card. But Evrart keeps me on the payroll. Just for the little things."
"Now, now..." His partner raises both hands in a calming gesture. "I'm sure the officer means it figuratively. Like a forensic technique or something, right?"
"Now-now, no need to get angry again, René. I'm sure the officer tried his best. It's not like there's a *boule*-kiosk here in Martinaise."
"Of course, officer, I hope I can help you." He nods enthusiastically. "What's on your mind?"
"Of course, officer, I mean I hope I can." He nods enthusiastically. "What's on your mind?"
"Of course, officer," he says with a smile. "Memories are all we have left."
"Of course, officer." He waits for you to speak.
"Officer!" He exclaims. "The mere sight of police in Martinaise makes me feel safer already. How can I help you?"
"Officer, I have a vivid imagination." He laughs again. "And like I said, I have a way with words. That's enough. No need to sink into politics."
"Officer, you must forgive Old René. Holding a conversation has always been... problematic with him." He flashes you a quick smile. "Try asking him something else."
"Officer," the other one jumps in. "Let's not get sidetracked here with this nasty business. I know you wanted something from old René or me. Let's talk about that instead."
"Officer..." The jolliness is gone from Gaston's face. "Care to play a game with a lonely old man?"
"Officer..." he looks up, all wrinkled, old and small. "I just can't do this right now. The Union... it just doesn't matter anymore."
"Oh absolutely..." He smiles as if reliving a pleasant memory. "At the mercy of a cocaine-snorting tyrant who emptied the treasury so he could sleep on a bed of gold?"
"Oh no, you have to get shot." He nods eagerly. "Repeatedly. And you need to get your hands bloody too. Really *really* bloody."
"Oh yes, René, yes..." The jolly man nods meekly. "Men were bigger, girls were prettier, and everyone was a *fascha* -- Lord, please bring those days back, if you can!"
"Oh yes."
"Oh, I didn't mean to imply there's something *wrong* with that," the jolly man says quickly. "I do it too. Everyone does it. It's an excellent side-thing."
"Oh, René..." He smiles wide and friendly. "If you only knew life beyond confrontations, conflict and extremities..."
"Oh, he would have liked that." The old man slowly shakes his head. "Violent lives ending violently... That's how he wanted to go. Sadly it was not the case."
"Oh, nothing official, I assure you. Just essays for the newspapers. About Martinaise and how things are and how they *could* be. Evrart and I have these long talks where..."
"Oh, officer..." Gaston is unfazed by the outburst. "It already got ugly nearly eighty years ago when the three of us were just learning to walk and talk."
"Oh, okay..." He seems to edge away from you. "It's perfectly alright. No harm done and it's really none of my business anyway."
"Oh, okay..." He seems to edge away from you. "Well *I* certainly have full confidence in your competence. And the future," he adds quickly.
"Oh, old Filippe was a *big* fan of the purple nose candy the nobility loved so much. A cocaine-connoisseur of sorts." He chuckles. "His egocentricity is borderline legendary."
"Oh, sweet Jeannie..." He gets a dreamy look in his eyes. "She was the finest woman in all of Revachol. Maybe the entire world."
"Oh, that's good, that's very good." He's visibly relieved. "You must have other business then?"
"Oh, uh... Well thank you, officer. It certainly lightened the mood." He laughs nervously. "Very cosy, like a little street fair almost."
"Oh, you're in for a treat, officer. Seeing the playful side of old René is about as rare as a red rainbow."
"Oh... sorry, officer... What do you want?"
"Oh..." He doesn't look up. "Good. Good for you, officer. I'm just wondering if René ever... never mind. Can I help you with something?"
"Oh..." He glances at the burnt writing. "Of course. I didn't think of it. Good job officer!"
"Oh..." His cheeks turn red again. "In many ways, yes. Like an honorary member. I attend meetings and parties. Help with little things. Evrart, Edgar, and the older *Débardeurs* all know me."
"Oh..." His eyes light up in understanding. "All that for a sandwich? I'm flattered, officer, but you can't have it. It's mine."
"Oh..." His eyes light up in understanding. "You went through all that trouble for my sandwich? I'm flattered, officer, but my answer is no. Now how else can I help you?"
"Oh..." he looks down for the longest time. "You're right of course, officer. It can't be good for my health. Please, take it off my hands."
"Oh? The goal is to throw your *boule*..." He holds out the orb. "... as close to the *cochonnet* as you can."
"On the Union-track?"
"Or god of sandwiches maybe?" he tries to pitch in. "But in the meanwhile, what can I do for you *here* and *now* officer?"
"Please, officer! Don't encourage him!" He quickly turns to René. "Do spare us the cocaine fairy tales. The RCM isn't interested in them."
"Real shame..." The old man nods, eyes still on the ground. He's not really paying attention to your words.
"René and I were both by her bedside when she..." He pauses, searching for the right word.
"René, tsk-tsk. It's the little pleasures. Life doesn't need to be a.... *mnjam mnjam*... a struggle."
"René, you are the angriest man in the world."
"René, you're a man with a fork in a world of soup. Please... let's just try to enjoy the game, alright?" The other one is eating a big sandwich.
"René, you're a man with a fork in a world of soup. Please... let's just try to enjoy the game, alright?" This one's still chewing on his sandwich.
"See, René, I told you he was one of the good guys." He chuckles. "You should have more faith in people."
"She could never make up her mind about anything. What to have for breakfast, favourite colour or which one of us to marry." The look in his eyes is happy and distant.
"She died of pneumonia two winters ago. It was a quiet passage. Peaceful." He smiles faintly.
"She was René's first girl, back when the prick was sixteen." He looks at the carabineer almost gently. "They were courting till he decided he'd rather die for some great *idéal* than just be hap---"
"She was always leaving one of us for the other, but never long enough to actually get married."
"So..." The sandwich-owner looks at you, obviously confused. "Is there something I can help you with instead or...?"
"Sometimes I thought he was wearing it just to piss me off." Gaston smiles a sad smile. "Now the joke's on him, 'cause he's gonna be buried without it."
"Sorry, officer, I'm sorry, I didn't mean it in a bad way," he continues cautiously. "But the sandwich is mine, I'm not gonna share it."
"Sorry, officer, but you're reading me all wrong." He chuckles. "I'm a man of peace and these kinds of bloody 'heroics' are only impressive to men like René himself. Certainly not to me."
"Sure, officer." He nods. "It's better for  René's flickering ticker too. Not that he'd ever admit anything there needs tinkering."
"Sure, officer." He smiles. "They are the good guys around here. What do you need?"
"Sweet sweet Jeannie..." He nods, smiling. "Ask away officer, I knew her all my life."
"Take it easy, René." The jolly one tries to defuse the situation. "This is just a misunderstanding, isn't it, officer? No harm done."
"Thank you officer," he nods, smiling wide. "For being a consummate professional. You'll have this case wrapped up in no time."
"Thank you, officer." The jolly man quickly takes the ball and bounces it in his hand. "This is really something... Honestly I think it's better than our old *boule* even!"
"That *would* certainly have been an improvement."
"That sounds *horrible*." A grimace of disgust runs over his jolly face. "You really don't know your way around the kitchen, officer. Food and politics don't mix."
"That's just the way things work around here," he declares merrily. "No reason to feel bad about it."
"That's the *cochonnet*." He points to a small wooden ball in the middle of the crater.
"The lady is Jeanne-Marie Beaulieu." Gaston speaks with a soft voice. "And she sure as hell wasn't a nobody."
"The only people who could stand to be around him were Jeannie and me..." He pauses. "She saw something in him when we were just kids, and..."
"The opponent has a right to re-measure if he has doubts about the result and..." He is trying to think of something else to say, but then -- seeing your beady eyes -- stops.
"The other one I took for myself." He looks at you defiantly. "No one knew him better than I did, and I want to remember that old cunt by something."
"The prick is gone," he replies, trying to smile. "I... I can barely believe it, but he's really gone."
"The prick survived all the bullets, swords and explosions just to die of a heart attack..." He sighs deeply. "Ironic, isn't it -- even his own bitter little heart couldn't stand him."
"Then the players aim to throw their *boules* as close to the *cochonnet* as possible. They must stay in the circle and keep both feet planted."
"There were many reasons, but mostly it was the communards. They called them 'The Bells of Revolution'." A sad smile passes his face.
"This... this isn't right, officer." He shakes his head. "René wanted to be buried in his uniform, but..."
"Those days and memories are gone." He nods and looks René with something resembling compassion.
"Ugh... it's not very good, officer. I'm an old man and sciatica is gnawing on my joints." There's a look of hopelessness in his eyes. "Some days the pain is almost too much..."
"Ugh... thank you, officer." He looks at you with disgust. "Please tell me there wasn't anything else?"
"Uh... *everything* really. I probably knew him better than..." He stops, realizing something. "You meant the teacup in the tree, didn't you? I don't know anything about him."
"Uh... thanks. Is there something we can help you with, officer?" He avoids your gaze.

"Uh..." Your keen interest is making him uncomfortable. "Then there's measuring the distance between the *boule* and the *cochonnet*. I always measure ours, but usually it's done by the player who threw last."
"Wait... But I thought..." The old-timer, visibly disappointed, pockets the sandwich and sighs. "I'd really like to get back to the game now, if there isn't anything else?"
"We all got to go some time, officer. Everyone I love is already there. Probably waiting for me." He smiles faintly. "I'm not afraid to die. It's been a good run and I really miss my friends..."
"We knew her, alright..." His friendly face lights up. "Lived on the same street our entire lives, just two houses apart. The three of us have been best friends since we were four."
"We've hated each other our entire lives. So much in fact that..." He falls silent and looks at you, eyes filling up with tears.
"Well yes, I mean... uh... no need to..." He raises his arms to signal you to stop. "I'm not sure I understand what's happening here, officer."

"Well, it's your own damn fault," the jolly man remarks. "You, we, the Coalition, Revachol -- whoever you wanna blame -- never finished the job. Officially the Party never surrendered. Of course they still hold influence."
"Well, officer, what did you think?" The jolly man leans forward, excited to hear your opinion.
"Well, you took one of them." He shakes his head. "Still can't believe he gave it to you, but that's how rigid he was. Once the offer carelessly left his lips it was irrefutable..."

"Well... first you draw a circle about a half a metre in diameter. We made ours out of rope," he explains. "Then the order of play is determined by a coin toss. You win it -- you get to throw the *cochonnet*."
"Well... technically *you* stole her from *me*, because we'd been pretty close ever since you two had that falling out over the ink you spilled over her pretty yellow dress..."
"What *Monseigneur Modestie* is not telling you is that he crawled over seven kilometres before the cavalrymen found him and Drysant. Two days later that was."
"What a prick," the jolly man declares, with a sigh. "The officer was addressing me, not you, *capitaine*. Where were we?"
"What are you talking about? You just executed a pretty much perfect pétanque throw!" His tone is full of admiration.
"What do you mean, officer?" He looks startled.
"What do you mean, officer?" There's a look of suspicion is his eyes.
"What is... actually never mind." He smiles a clever smile "I'm sure there's *something* I can help you with, officer."
"What? No!" He gasps, looking like he's about to cry. "Old angry René doesn't even have taste buds -- it would be a complete..."
"What?!" The man tries to act surprised.
"Would you like to play alone tomorrow?"
"Writing work mostly," he smiles. "Occasionally he needs something written and I happen to have a way with words, people say."
"Yes, officer, yes!!! I swear, I don't know anything else about pétanque! It's all I know, I swear!"
"Yes, officer." He proudly displays his culinary miracle. It is magnificent.
"Yes, yes, the good old days. The all or nothing days."
"Yes, yes. I'm sorry, officer." The senior is visibly shaking before you.
"Yes, yes... and the taste?" He leans even closer. "How was the taste?"
"Yes. I... I loved that angry prick. He didn't deserve it, but I did." He wipes his eyes with a sleeve. "You know what his last words to me were?"
"Yes..." A strange expression runs across his wrinkled face, then vanishes without trace.
"Yes..." A strange expression runs across his wrinkled face, when he repeats: "in peace."
"Yes?" he looks up. "What about, René?"
"You are the angriest man I know, René."
"You must forgive mean old René, officer!" The other one jumps in. "He can't stop being himself more than a scorpion can stop being a sco..."
"You see, officer, René is the kind of man who'd rather die than admit he needs medical assistance or -- god forbid -- seek it. A real man's man. He's just gonna *ride it out*."
"You were like a dark cloud sucking the joy out of every living thing around you, and you..." He quickly glances at you. "You... *hurt* her."
"You'll put that knowledge to good use in twenty... I mean fifty years. I'm sure of that officer."
